original_question: Let K be an adequate Smyth category. If X is a K-determined T0 space, is its Smyth power space PS(X) again K-determined?
target_in_paper: Section 7, Question 7.20 (the converse direction left open after Theorem 7.19).
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper's exact open problem very closely: it has the right hypotheses ('K' adequate and Smyth, 'X' a K-determined T0 space), the right construction (the Smyth power space P_S(X)), and the right preservation question ('again K-determined?'). It is essentially a near-verbatim restatement of Question 7.20.
missing_details: The paper takes K to be a full subcategory of Top_0 containing Sob; that ambient categorical setting is implicit in the draft.
'Adequate' should be unpacked: for every T0 space X, the lower Vietoris space on the family of closed K-determined subsets of X is a K-space.
'Smyth category' should be unpacked: whenever Y is a K-space, its Smyth power space P_S(Y) is again a K-space.

'K-determined' should be defined explicitly: a subset A of X is K-determined if for every continuous map f:X -> Y into a K-space Y, there exists a unique point y in Y such that cl_Y(f(A)) = cl_Y({y}); X is K-determined iff every irreducible closed subset of X is K-determined.
P_S(X) should be defined explicitly as the space of nonempty compact saturated subsets of X equipped with the upper Vietoris topology.
To make the question fully stand-alone, it helps to note that this is exactly the converse of Theorem 7.19, which proves that if P_S(X) is K-determined then X is K-determined.
refined_question: Let K be a full subcategory of Top_0 containing Sob. For a T0 space X, call a subset A ⊆ X K-determined if for every continuous map f:X -> Y into a K-space Y, there exists a unique point y in Y such that cl_Y(f(A)) = cl_Y({y}); call X K-determined if every irreducible closed subset of X is K-determined. Assume moreover that K is adequate, meaning that for every T0 space X the lower Vietoris space on the family of closed K-determined subsets of X is a K-space, and that K is a Smyth category, meaning that P_S(Y) is a K-space for every K-space Y. If X is a K-determined T0 space, must its Smyth power space P_S(X) - the space of nonempty compact saturated subsets of X equipped with the upper Vietoris topology - also be K-determined?
equivalent_formulation: Under the same hypotheses on K and X, is it true that X is K-determined if and only if P_S(X) is K-determined?
justification: The draft is already targeting the exact statement asked in the paper: Question 7.20 in Section 7 asks whether K-determinedness is preserved by the Smyth power-space construction for adequate Smyth categories. The only missing pieces are the paper's definitions of K-determined (Definition 5.5), adequate (Definition 7.3), and Smyth category (Definition 7.18), plus the definition of the Smyth power space from Section 2. Theorem 7.19 proves the reverse implication P_S(X) K-determined => X K-determined, so the open problem is precisely the converse and not a broader neighboring question.
